background: The Toronto-Dominion Bank is Canada's second-largest bank, funded by Canadian and US deposits and lending on Canadian mortgages and to businesses, with a large US retail bank along the east coast that has been under a regulatory asset cap after its anti-money-laundering failures.
synthesis: Rated A+ on average across all three, the weakest of them at A, all on a stable outlook; the last move was a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 23 Oct 2024. Capital is strong, with CET1 of 14.3% in the top quarter of Canadian banks, though it has fallen 0.6 points since 30 Apr 2025. No leverage or liquidity figures are carried in the figures to 31 Jul 2026.
